_meta: Canonical fix patterns for cppcheck/MISRA rules. risk_level comes from rule_policy, not from this file. Injected into chunk JSON per-rule via lookup_fix_pattern().

unreadVariable.fix: Remove the unread variable or use its value in a meaningful expression.
unreadVariable.example: result = calc(x); /* fix: unreadVariable — use return value */
unreadVariable.caution: Verify the variable is not intentionally unused for debugging or assertion.

constVariable.fix: Add const qualifier to the variable declaration.
constVariable.example: const uint8_t val = 10; /* fix: constVariable — added const qualifier */

uninitvar.fix: Initialize the variable at its declaration point.
uninitvar.example: int count = 0; /* fix: uninitvar — initialized to zero */
uninitvar.caution: Choose the correct initial value; zero may not always be appropriate.
uninitvar.pitfalls: Masking a real logic error with a default value can hide bugs. Verify the intended initial state.
uninitvar.context_notes: In safety-critical code, prefer explicit initialization matching the domain's default state.

uninitStructMember.fix: Initialize the struct member, preferably via memset or designated initializer.
uninitStructMember.example: memset(&obj, 0, sizeof(obj)); /* fix: uninitStructMember — zero-init struct */
uninitStructMember.caution: Verify that zero is the correct initial value for all members.
uninitStructMember.pitfalls: Struct may contain pointer members where zero-init creates NULL pointers; ensure callers handle this.
uninitStructMember.context_notes: In embedded code, prefer designated initializers over memset for structs with non-trivial layouts.

nullPointer.fix: Add NULL guard before the first dereference of the pointer.
nullPointer.example: if (ptr == NULL) { return ERR_NULL; } /* fix: nullPointer — added NULL guard */
nullPointer.caution: Verify all code paths that reach this dereference.
nullPointer.pitfalls: Adding a NULL guard changes control flow. If the pointer should never be NULL by contract, consider assert instead.
nullPointer.context_notes: In safety-critical code, prefer returning an explicit error code rather than silently continuing.

nullPointerRedundantCheck.fix: Remove the redundant NULL check, or restructure the logic so the check is consistent.
nullPointerRedundantCheck.example: /* fix: nullPointerRedundantCheck — removed redundant NULL check (already dereferenced above) */
nullPointerRedundantCheck.caution: Verify that the earlier dereference truly guarantees non-NULL at this point.

bufferAccessOutOfBounds.fix: Fix the buffer size or clamp the access index to stay within bounds.
bufferAccessOutOfBounds.example: if (idx < sizeof(buf)) { buf[idx] = val; } /* fix: bufferAccessOutOfBounds — bounds check */
bufferAccessOutOfBounds.caution: Verify the buffer size calculation accounts for all possible input sizes.
bufferAccessOutOfBounds.pitfalls: Off-by-one errors are common. Double-check whether the bound should be < or <=.
bufferAccessOutOfBounds.context_notes: In safety-critical code, consider adding runtime assertions for buffer bounds.

arrayIndexOutOfBounds.fix: Ensure the array index is within [0, array_size - 1].
arrayIndexOutOfBounds.example: if (i < ARRAY_SIZE) { arr[i] = v; } /* fix: arrayIndexOutOfBounds — added bounds check */
arrayIndexOutOfBounds.caution: Verify the array size constant matches the actual declaration.
arrayIndexOutOfBounds.pitfalls: The index expression may depend on external input; validate at the source.
arrayIndexOutOfBounds.context_notes: Prefer compile-time array size macros (e.g., sizeof(arr)/sizeof(arr[0])) over hardcoded constants.

memoryLeak.fix: Free the allocated memory on all code paths, including error paths.
memoryLeak.example: free(buf); buf = NULL; /* fix: memoryLeak — freed allocation on error path */
memoryLeak.caution: Ensure the pointer is not used after free.
memoryLeak.pitfalls: Adding free on error paths may introduce double-free if the pointer is aliased.
memoryLeak.context_notes: In embedded systems, consider whether dynamic allocation should be replaced with static allocation.

resourceLeak.fix: Close or release the resource on all code paths, including error paths.
resourceLeak.example: fclose(fp); /* fix: resourceLeak — closed file on error path */
resourceLeak.caution: Ensure the resource handle is valid before closing.
resourceLeak.pitfalls: If the resource handle is shared, closing it may affect other users.
resourceLeak.context_notes: Consider using RAII-style cleanup patterns (goto cleanup) for multiple resources.

doubleFree.fix: Remove the duplicate free call or set pointer to NULL after first free.
doubleFree.example: free(ptr); ptr = NULL; /* fix: doubleFree — set to NULL after free to prevent double-free */
doubleFree.pitfalls: The second free may be on a different code path; trace all paths to the pointer.
doubleFree.context_notes: In safety-critical code, always set pointer to NULL immediately after free.

deallocDealloc.fix: Remove the duplicate deallocation or guard with a NULL check.
deallocDealloc.example: if (ptr != NULL) { free(ptr); ptr = NULL; } /* fix: deallocDealloc — guarded dealloc */
deallocDealloc.pitfalls: Multiple deallocation paths may indicate a deeper ownership confusion.
deallocDealloc.context_notes: Consider consolidating cleanup into a single function to prevent double deallocation.

useClosedFile.fix: Check file status before use, or restructure to not use the file after close.
useClosedFile.example: /* fix: useClosedFile — moved fclose() after all file operations */
useClosedFile.pitfalls: Reordering file operations may change the output or error handling sequence.
useClosedFile.context_notes: Ensure error handling does not close the file prematurely.

leakNoVarFunctionCall.fix: Capture the allocated pointer from the function call and free it when done.
leakNoVarFunctionCall.example: char *tmp = strdup(s); use(tmp); free(tmp); /* fix: leakNoVarFunctionCall — captured and freed */
leakNoVarFunctionCall.caution: Ensure the captured pointer is freed on all code paths.

leakReturnValNotUsed.fix: Capture the return value and free/release it, or pass it to the caller.
leakReturnValNotUsed.example: char *p = alloc_func(); /* fix: leakReturnValNotUsed — captured return value */
leakReturnValNotUsed.caution: If the return value is intentionally discarded, document why and suppress the warning.

returnLocalVariable.fix: Return a copy of the data, or allocate on the heap and document ownership.
returnLocalVariable.example: char *result = strdup(local_buf); return result; /* fix: returnLocalVariable — heap copy */
returnLocalVariable.pitfalls: Heap allocation shifts ownership responsibility to the caller.
returnLocalVariable.context_notes: In embedded code, prefer caller-provided buffers over heap allocation.

returnReference.fix: Return a copy instead of a reference to a local variable.
returnReference.example: return local_val; /* fix: returnReference — return by value, not by reference */
returnReference.pitfalls: For large objects, returning by value may have performance implications.

autoVariables.fix: Do not store address of auto (stack) variable in a pointer that outlives the scope.
autoVariables.example: static int val = 0; *out = &val; /* fix: autoVariables — use static or heap storage */
autoVariables.pitfalls: Using static storage makes the function non-reentrant.
autoVariables.context_notes: In multithreaded or interrupt context, static storage can cause data races.

danglingTemporaryLifetime.fix: Extend the object's lifetime by storing it in a named variable.
danglingTemporaryLifetime.example: struct S obj = make_s(); use(&obj); /* fix: danglingTemporaryLifetime — extended lifetime */
danglingTemporaryLifetime.pitfalls: Ensure the named variable lives long enough for all uses of its address.

comparisonError.fix: Fix the comparison operator or operand to match the intended logic.
comparisonError.example: if (a < b) /* fix: comparisonError — corrected comparison from <= to < */
comparisonError.caution: Verify the intended boundary condition (< vs <= vs == vs !=).

returnAddressOfAutoVariable.fix: Do not return the address of a local (auto) variable; use static storage or heap allocation.
returnAddressOfAutoVariable.example: static int val; return &​val; /* fix: returnAddressOfAutoVariable — returned address of static instead of auto */
returnAddressOfAutoVariable.pitfalls: Using static storage makes the function non-reentrant.
returnAddressOfAutoVariable.context_notes: In multithreaded code, prefer caller-provided output buffers over static storage.

autovarInvalidDeallocation.fix: Do not call free/delete on a stack-allocated (auto) variable.
autovarInvalidDeallocation.example: /* fix: autovarInvalidDeallocation — removed free() on stack variable */
autovarInvalidDeallocation.pitfalls: Freeing stack memory causes undefined behavior and likely crashes.
autovarInvalidDeallocation.context_notes: Verify whether the variable was intended to be heap-allocated.

returnAddressOfFunctionParameter.fix: Do not return the address of a function parameter; copy to heap or use caller-provided buffer.
returnAddressOfFunctionParameter.example: memcpy(out, &param, sizeof(param)); /* fix: returnAddressOfFunctionParameter — copied to caller buffer */
returnAddressOfFunctionParameter.pitfalls: Function parameters are stack-allocated and become invalid after return.

negativeMemoryAllocationSize.fix: Ensure the allocation size argument is non-negative; use size_t type.
negativeMemoryAllocationSize.example: size_t sz = (size_t)len; void *p = malloc(sz); /* fix: negativeMemoryAllocationSize — ensured non-negative size */
negativeMemoryAllocationSize.caution: A signed-to-unsigned conversion of a negative value produces a very large allocation.
negativeMemoryAllocationSize.pitfalls: Negative sizes wrapped to unsigned may exhaust memory or succeed with a huge allocation.
negativeMemoryAllocationSize.context_notes: Validate the size value at the source before passing to allocation functions.

mismatchSize.fix: Ensure the size argument to allocation/copy functions matches the target type size.
mismatchSize.example: int *p = malloc(n * sizeof(int)); /* fix: mismatchSize — matched sizeof to target type */
mismatchSize.caution: Using sizeof(pointer) instead of sizeof(*pointer) is a common mistake.

negativeArraySize.fix: Ensure the array size expression is non-negative.
negativeArraySize.example: /* fix: negativeArraySize — validated array size is non-negative before use */
negativeArraySize.pitfalls: Negative array size is undefined behavior in C.

negativeIndex.fix: Ensure the array index is non-negative before use.
negativeIndex.example: if (idx >= 0) { val = arr[idx]; } /* fix: negativeIndex — added non-negative index check */
negativeIndex.caution: The index expression may come from untrusted input; validate at the source.
negativeIndex.pitfalls: Negative indices access memory before the array, causing undefined behavior.

insecureCmdLineArgs.fix: Validate and bound-check command-line arguments before copying into fixed-size buffers.
insecureCmdLineArgs.example: strncpy(buf, argv[1], sizeof(buf) - 1U); buf[sizeof(buf) - 1U] = '\0'; /* fix: insecureCmdLineArgs — bounded copy */
insecureCmdLineArgs.pitfalls: Unbounded strcpy of argv can overflow stack buffers.
insecureCmdLineArgs.context_notes: In embedded systems, command-line arguments may not apply; verify usage context.

integerOverflow.fix: Widen operands or add overflow check before the arithmetic operation.
integerOverflow.example: uint32_t r = (uint32_t)a * (uint32_t)b; /* fix: integerOverflow — widened operands */
integerOverflow.caution: Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C.
integerOverflow.pitfalls: Overflow checks after the operation are too late; the UB has already occurred.
integerOverflow.context_notes: Use compiler builtins (__builtin_mul_overflow) or manual pre-checks for safety-critical code.

floatConversionOverflow.fix: Add range check before converting floating-point value to integer type.
floatConversionOverflow.example: if (f >= INT_MIN && f <= INT_MAX) { i = (int)f; } /* fix: floatConversionOverflow — range check */
floatConversionOverflow.pitfalls: Float-to-int conversion overflow is undefined behavior.
floatConversionOverflow.context_notes: Consider the target integer type's range limits (INT_MIN/INT_MAX, UINT_MAX, etc.).

uninitstring.fix: Initialize the string buffer before use (e.g., memset or assign a null terminator).
uninitstring.example: char buf[64] = {0}; /* fix: uninitstring — zero-initialized string buffer */
uninitstring.caution: Ensure the initialization covers the full buffer length.

memleak.fix: Free the allocated memory on all code paths, including error paths.
memleak.example: free(ptr); ptr = NULL; /* fix: memleak — freed allocation on all paths */
memleak.caution: Ensure the pointer is not used after free.
memleak.pitfalls: Error paths are the most common source of memory leaks.
memleak.context_notes: Use a goto-cleanup pattern to centralize memory release.

memleakOnRealloc.fix: Use a temporary pointer for realloc; only update the original on success.
memleakOnRealloc.example: void *tmp = realloc(ptr, new_sz); if (tmp != NULL) { ptr = tmp; } /* fix: memleakOnRealloc — safe realloc pattern */
memleakOnRealloc.pitfalls: If realloc fails and the result is assigned directly to ptr, the original memory is leaked.
memleakOnRealloc.context_notes: In safety-critical code, avoid realloc entirely; use static allocation.

deallocret.fix: Do not return freed/deallocated memory; restructure to return before free or copy data.
deallocret.example: int result = *ptr; free(ptr); return result; /* fix: deallocret — captured value before free */
deallocret.pitfalls: Returning a pointer to freed memory causes use-after-free in the caller.

deallocuse.fix: Do not use memory after it has been freed; restructure code to use before free.
deallocuse.example: use(ptr); free(ptr); ptr = NULL; /* fix: deallocuse — moved use before free */
deallocuse.pitfalls: Use-after-free is undefined behavior and a security vulnerability (CWE-416).
deallocuse.context_notes: Set pointer to NULL immediately after free to catch accidental reuse.

mismatchAllocDealloc.fix: Match allocation and deallocation functions (malloc/free, new/delete, new[]/delete[]).
mismatchAllocDealloc.example: free(ptr); /* fix: mismatchAllocDealloc — matched free() with malloc() */
mismatchAllocDealloc.pitfalls: Mismatched alloc/dealloc causes undefined behavior and memory corruption.
mismatchAllocDealloc.context_notes: In C code, always pair malloc/calloc/realloc with free.

unusedAllocatedMemory.fix: Remove the allocation if the memory is never used, or use it in a meaningful expression.
unusedAllocatedMemory.caution: The allocation may be intentionally reserved for future use; verify intent.

assignBoolToPointer.fix: Do not assign a boolean value to a pointer; use NULL or a valid address.
assignBoolToPointer.example: ptr = NULL; /* fix: assignBoolToPointer — assigned NULL instead of boolean */
assignBoolToPointer.pitfalls: Assigning true/false to a pointer creates an invalid pointer value.

invalidFunctionArg.fix: Pass a valid argument value to the function as documented by its contract.
invalidFunctionArg.example: /* fix: invalidFunctionArg — corrected argument to valid range */
invalidFunctionArg.caution: Check the function documentation for valid input ranges.
invalidFunctionArg.pitfalls: Invalid arguments may cause undefined behavior or silent data corruption.

invalidFunctionArgBool.fix: Pass the correct type (bool vs int) to the function parameter.
invalidFunctionArgBool.example: /* fix: invalidFunctionArgBool — passed boolean value instead of integer */
invalidFunctionArgBool.caution: Verify the function signature expects a boolean parameter.

strPlusChar.fix: Use string concatenation instead of adding a char to a string pointer (pointer arithmetic).
strPlusChar.example: strncat(str, &ch, 1); /* fix: strPlusChar — proper string concatenation */
strPlusChar.pitfalls: Adding a char to a string pointer advances the pointer by the char's ASCII value, not appending.

ignoredReturnValue.fix: Use the return value or explicitly cast to (void) if intentionally discarding.
ignoredReturnValue.example: (void)printf("msg"); /* fix: ignoredReturnValue — cast unused return to void */
ignoredReturnValue.caution: If the function can fail, prefer capturing and checking the return value.
ignoredReturnValue.context_notes: In safety-critical code, always check return values of functions that can fail.

wrongPipeParameterSize.fix: Pass the correct size argument to pipe() system call.
wrongPipeParameterSize.example: int fds[2]; pipe(fds); /* fix: wrongPipeParameterSize — correct array size for pipe */
wrongPipeParameterSize.caution: pipe() requires an array of exactly 2 int elements.

memsetFloat.fix: Do not use memset on floating-point variables; assign directly.
memsetFloat.example: float f = 0.0f; /* fix: memsetFloat — direct assignment instead of memset */
memsetFloat.pitfalls: memset fills bytes; all-zero bytes is not necessarily 0.0 for float on all platforms.
memsetFloat.context_notes: IEEE 754 guarantees +0.0 is all-zero bits, but MISRA forbids relying on representation.

sizeofCalculation.fix: Move the calculation outside of sizeof(); sizeof evaluates type, not value.
sizeofCalculation.example: size_t s = sizeof(int); int r = a + b; /* fix: sizeofCalculation — moved calculation outside sizeof */
sizeofCalculation.pitfalls: Calculations inside sizeof are not evaluated at runtime (except VLAs in C99+).

strncatUsage.fix: Use the remaining buffer space as the size argument, not the total buffer size.
strncatUsage.example: strncat(buf, src, sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf) - 1U); /* fix: strncatUsage — correct remaining size */
strncatUsage.pitfalls: strncat's third argument is the max chars to append, not the total buffer size.
strncatUsage.context_notes: Prefer snprintf for safer string assembly.

selfInitialization.fix: Initialize the variable with a valid value, not with itself.
selfInitialization.example: int x = 0; /* fix: selfInitialization — replaced self-init with valid value */
selfInitialization.pitfalls: Self-initialization reads an uninitialized value, causing undefined behavior.

uninitdata.fix: Initialize the allocated data before use (memset or explicit assignment).
uninitdata.example: memset(ptr, 0, size); /* fix: uninitdata — zero-initialized allocated data */
uninitdata.caution: Verify that zero is the correct initial value for the data.
uninitdata.context_notes: calloc() zero-initializes automatically; prefer it over malloc+memset when appropriate.

uninitMemberVar.fix: Initialize the member variable in the constructor or at declaration.
uninitMemberVar.example: /* fix: uninitMemberVar — initialized member variable to default value */
uninitMemberVar.caution: Choose an appropriate initial value matching the domain semantics.

unusedStructMember.fix: Remove the unused struct member or use it in a meaningful expression.
unusedStructMember.example: /* fix: unusedStructMember — removed unused member 'flags' from struct */
unusedStructMember.caution: The member may be required for alignment, padding, or ABI compatibility.

IOWithoutPositioning.fix: Add fseek/fsetpos/rewind between read and write operations on the same file.
IOWithoutPositioning.example: fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_CUR); /* fix: IOWithoutPositioning — added positioning between I/O ops */
IOWithoutPositioning.pitfalls: Mixing read and write without positioning causes undefined behavior per C standard.

readWriteOnlyFile.fix: Open the file with the correct mode that permits reading.
readWriteOnlyFile.example: fp = fopen(path, "r+"); /* fix: readWriteOnlyFile — opened with read-write mode */
readWriteOnlyFile.pitfalls: Reading from a write-only file causes undefined behavior.

writeReadOnlyFile.fix: Open the file with the correct mode that permits writing.
writeReadOnlyFile.example: fp = fopen(path, "r+"); /* fix: writeReadOnlyFile — opened with read-write mode */
writeReadOnlyFile.pitfalls: Writing to a read-only file causes undefined behavior.

wrongPrintfScanfArgNum.fix: Match the number of format specifiers with the number of arguments.
wrongPrintfScanfArgNum.example: printf("%d %d", a, b); /* fix: wrongPrintfScanfArgNum — matched arg count to format */
wrongPrintfScanfArgNum.pitfalls: Too few arguments causes undefined behavior; too many are silently ignored.
wrongPrintfScanfArgNum.context_notes: Use compiler warnings (-Wformat) to catch format/argument mismatches at compile time.

invalidScanfFormatWidth.fix: Add or correct the width specifier in scanf format string to match buffer size.
invalidScanfFormatWidth.example: scanf("%63s", buf); /* fix: invalidScanfFormatWidth — width matches buf size minus 1 */
invalidScanfFormatWidth.pitfalls: Missing width specifier in scanf allows unbounded input, causing buffer overflow.

sprintfOverlappingData.fix: Ensure source and destination buffers do not overlap in sprintf calls.
sprintfOverlappingData.example: char tmp[64]; sprintf(tmp, "%s_suffix", buf); strcpy(buf, tmp); /* fix: sprintfOverlappingData — used temp buffer */
sprintfOverlappingData.pitfalls: Overlapping source and destination in sprintf is undefined behavior.

invalidscanf.fix: Add a width specifier to scanf %s format to prevent buffer overflow.
invalidscanf.example: scanf("%63s", buf); /* fix: invalidscanf — added width limit to scanf format */
invalidscanf.pitfalls: scanf %s without width limit can overflow any fixed-size buffer.

shiftNegative.fix: Ensure the shift amount is non-negative.
shiftNegative.example: uint32_t r = val << 4U; /* fix: shiftNegative — ensured non-negative shift amount */
shiftNegative.pitfalls: Shifting by a negative amount is undefined behavior in C.
shiftNegative.context_notes: Cast shift amounts to unsigned to prevent accidental negative values.

shiftTooManyBits.fix: Ensure the shift amount is less than the bit width of the type.
shiftTooManyBits.example: uint32_t r = val << (n % 32U); /* fix: shiftTooManyBits — clamped shift to type width */
shiftTooManyBits.pitfalls: Shifting by >= bit width is undefined behavior.
shiftTooManyBits.context_notes: For uint32_t, valid shift range is 0..31; for uint16_t, 0..15.

shiftTooManyBitsSigned.fix: Ensure the shift amount is less than the bit width of the signed type, and the value is non-negative.
shiftTooManyBitsSigned.example: int32_t r = val << 4; /* fix: shiftTooManyBitsSigned — shift within signed type width */
shiftTooManyBitsSigned.pitfalls: Shifting a negative signed value or shifting into the sign bit is undefined behavior.
shiftTooManyBitsSigned.context_notes: Prefer unsigned types for bitwise operations to avoid signed shift UB.

zerodiv.fix: Add a zero-check before the division/modulo operation.
zerodiv.example: if (divisor != 0) { result = a / divisor; } /* fix: zerodiv — added zero-division guard */
zerodiv.pitfalls: Division by zero is undefined behavior and typically causes a hardware exception.
zerodiv.context_notes: In safety-critical code, return an explicit error code when divisor is zero.

zerodivcond.fix: Review the condition: either the division by zero is possible, or the check is redundant.
zerodivcond.example: if (d != 0) { r = a / d; } /* fix: zerodivcond — ensured divisor check covers division */
zerodivcond.caution: This may indicate a logic error where the zero check and division are on different code paths.

unknownEvaluationOrder.fix: Split the expression so each sub-expression with side effects is in a separate statement.
unknownEvaluationOrder.example: int a = f(); int b = g(); result = a + b; /* fix: unknownEvaluationOrder — separated side effects */
unknownEvaluationOrder.pitfalls: Unsequenced side effects cause undefined behavior (e.g., x = x++ is UB).
unknownEvaluationOrder.context_notes: C11 defines sequence points more precisely; still prefer clear separation.

knownConditionTrueFalse.fix: Review and fix the condition that is always true or always false; remove dead branch if intended.
knownConditionTrueFalse.example: /* fix: knownConditionTrueFalse — removed always-true condition and dead else branch */
knownConditionTrueFalse.caution: An always-true/false condition may indicate a logic error or missing variable update.
knownConditionTrueFalse.context_notes: If intentional (e.g., configuration-based), document with a comment.

unreachableCode.fix: Remove the unreachable code or fix the control flow so it becomes reachable.
unreachableCode.example: /* fix: unreachableCode — removed unreachable code after return */
unreachableCode.caution: Unreachable code may be defensive or for future use; verify intent before removal.

redundantAssignment.fix: Remove the redundant assignment that is overwritten before being read.
redundantAssignment.caution: The assignment may have intended side effects (e.g., volatile); verify before removing.

constStatement.fix: Remove the statement with no side effect, or fix it to perform the intended action.
constStatement.example: /* fix: constStatement — removed or corrected statement with no effect */
constStatement.caution: The statement may be an incomplete expression (missing assignment or function call).

unusedFunction.fix: Remove the unused function or mark it as used.
unusedFunction.caution: The function may be used by other translation units or via function pointer; verify linkage.

unassignedVariable.fix: Assign a value to the variable before it is used, or remove it if unnecessary.
unassignedVariable.example: int count = 0; /* fix: unassignedVariable — assigned initial value */
unassignedVariable.caution: The variable may be set conditionally; ensure all paths assign before use.

duplicateBreak.caution: Verify the second break was not intended for a different code path after refactoring.

selfAssignment.fix: Remove the self-assignment or fix to assign the intended source variable.
selfAssignment.caution: May indicate a typo where a different source variable was intended.

duplicateExpression.fix: Fix the duplicate operand to the intended different operand.
duplicateExpression.example: if (a != b) /* fix: duplicateExpression — corrected duplicate operand */
duplicateExpression.caution: Duplicate expressions in comparisons (a == a) may indicate a copy-paste error.

stringLiteralWrite.fix: Do not write to a string literal; use a char array instead.
stringLiteralWrite.example: char buf[] = "hello"; buf[0] = 'H'; /* fix: stringLiteralWrite — writable char array */
stringLiteralWrite.pitfalls: Writing to a string literal is undefined behavior and may cause segfault.
stringLiteralWrite.context_notes: String literals are stored in read-only memory on most platforms.

uselessAssignmentArg.fix: Remove the useless assignment to a function argument, or use the modified value.
uselessAssignmentArg.example: /* fix: uselessAssignmentArg — removed useless assignment to parameter */
uselessAssignmentArg.caution: In C, modifying a parameter does not affect the caller's variable.

misra-c2012-2.1.fix: Remove unreachable code or fix the control flow so the code becomes reachable.
misra-c2012-2.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-2.1 — removed unreachable code after return */
misra-c2012-2.1.caution: Unreachable code may be intentional for defensive programming; verify intent.
misra-c2012-2.1.pitfalls: Removing code after a conditional return may break future maintenance if the condition changes.
misra-c2012-2.1.context_notes: In safety-critical code, unreachable code may indicate a logic error in the control flow.

misra-c2012-2.2.fix: Remove dead code (code whose result is never used).
misra-c2012-2.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-2.2 — removed dead assignment to 'x' */

misra-c2012-2.4.fix: Remove the unused tag declaration, or use it.
misra-c2012-2.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-2.4 — removed unused struct tag 'S' */
misra-c2012-2.4.caution: The tag may be used in other translation units via a shared header.

misra-c2012-2.5.caution: The macro may be used by other translation units or configuration headers.

misra-c2012-2.6.caution: The label may be part of incomplete error-handling refactoring.

misra-c2012-2.7.fix: Cast the unused parameter to (void) to suppress the warning.

misra-c2012-3.1.fix: Remove or escape the /* or // sequence inside a comment.
misra-c2012-3.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-3.1 — removed nested comment sequence */
misra-c2012-3.1.caution: Ensure the comment content is still correct after modification.

misra-c2012-3.2.fix: Remove the line splice (backslash-newline) inside a // comment.
misra-c2012-3.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-3.2 — removed line splice in comment */

misra-c2012-4.1.fix: Use only valid escape sequences (\n, \t, \0, etc.) or hex escapes.
misra-c2012-4.1.example: char c = '\x41'; /* fix: misra-c2012-4.1 — used hex escape instead of octal */
misra-c2012-4.1.pitfalls: Incorrect escape sequences can silently produce wrong character values.
misra-c2012-4.1.context_notes: In embedded displays, verify the character encoding matches the target hardware.

misra-c2012-4.2.fix: Replace trigraph sequences (??X) with the intended character.

misra-c2012-5.1.fix: Shorten the external identifier to ensure uniqueness within the first 31 characters.
misra-c2012-5.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-5.1 — shortened identifier for 31-char uniqueness */
misra-c2012-5.1.caution: Renaming an external identifier affects all translation units that reference it.

misra-c2012-5.2.fix: Rename the inner-scope identifier to avoid hiding the outer-scope identifier.
misra-c2012-5.2.example: int inner_val = 0; /* fix: misra-c2012-5.2 — renamed to avoid hiding outer 'val' */
misra-c2012-5.2.caution: Ensure all references to the renamed identifier are updated consistently.

misra-c2012-5.3.fix: Rename the identifier to avoid hiding a broader-scope name.
misra-c2012-5.3.example: int local_count = 0; /* fix: misra-c2012-5.3 — renamed to avoid hiding 'count' */
misra-c2012-5.3.caution: Check that the new name does not conflict with other identifiers in scope.

misra-c2012-5.4.fix: Rename the macro to ensure identifier uniqueness.
misra-c2012-5.4.example: #define MOD_MAX_SIZE (100) /* fix: misra-c2012-5.4 — prefixed macro for uniqueness */
misra-c2012-5.4.caution: Macro renaming may affect all files that include the header.

misra-c2012-5.5.fix: Rename the macro to avoid clashing with identifiers in other namespaces.
misra-c2012-5.5.example: #define MOD_STATUS (0) /* fix: misra-c2012-5.5 — prefixed to avoid namespace clash */
misra-c2012-5.5.caution: Update all references to the renamed macro across headers.

misra-c2012-8.1.fix: Add explicit type specifiers to all declarations (no implicit int).

misra-c2012-8.2.fix: Add a function prototype with named parameters for all functions.

misra-c2012-8.3.fix: Ensure all declarations of a function/object use compatible types.

misra-c2012-8.4.fix: Add or reconcile a visible forward declaration to match the definition.
misra-c2012-8.4.example: extern uint8_t foo(void); /* fix: misra-c2012-8.4 — added compatible declaration */
misra-c2012-8.4.caution: Ensure the declaration is in a shared header, not duplicated locally.
misra-c2012-8.4.pitfalls: Mismatched declarations across translation units cause silent undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-8.4.context_notes: In large projects, use a lint or build check to detect declaration mismatches.

misra-c2012-8.5.fix: Ensure an external object/function is defined in exactly one translation unit.
misra-c2012-8.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-8.5 — moved definition to single .c file, kept extern in .h */
misra-c2012-8.5.caution: Moving definitions may affect link order and initialization.

misra-c2012-8.6.fix: Provide exactly one external definition for each identifier with external linkage.
misra-c2012-8.6.caution: Removing a duplicate definition may break other translation units.

misra-c2012-8.7.fix: Reduce scope: add static qualifier if the object/function is only used in one file.
misra-c2012-8.7.example: static int helper(void) { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-8.7 — added static for file scope */
misra-c2012-8.7.caution: Verify the identifier is truly not referenced from other translation units.

misra-c2012-8.8.fix: Add static keyword for functions/objects with internal linkage.
misra-c2012-8.8.example: static void internal_func(void); /* fix: misra-c2012-8.8 — added static */
misra-c2012-8.8.caution: Verify the function is not referenced from other files.

misra-c2012-8.9.fix: Move the object declaration to the narrowest possible scope (block scope).
misra-c2012-8.9.example: void f(void) { int local = 0; /* fix: misra-c2012-8.9 — moved to block scope */ }
misra-c2012-8.9.caution: Moving a variable to a narrower scope changes its lifetime and may affect initialization order.

misra-c2012-8.10.fix: Add static qualifier to inline functions with internal linkage.
misra-c2012-8.10.example: static inline int max(int a, int b) { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-8.10 — added static */
misra-c2012-8.10.caution: Verify the inline function is not needed externally.

misra-c2012-8.11.fix: Add explicit size to extern array declarations.
misra-c2012-8.11.example: extern uint8_t buf[BUF_SIZE]; /* fix: misra-c2012-8.11 — added array size */

misra-c2012-8.12.fix: Specify all or no explicit values for enum members (do not mix).
misra-c2012-8.12.example: enum State { IDLE = 0, RUN = 1, STOP = 2 }; /* fix: misra-c2012-8.12 — all values explicit */

misra-c2012-8.13.fix: Add const qualifier to pointer parameter when the pointed-to data is not modified.
misra-c2012-8.13.example: void foo(const uint8_t *p); /* fix: misra-c2012-8.13 — added const qualifier */
misra-c2012-8.13.caution: Verify the function implementation does not modify data through this pointer.

misra-c2012-8.14.fix: Remove the restrict qualifier from the pointer declaration.
misra-c2012-8.14.example: void copy(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src); /* fix: misra-c2012-8.14 — removed restrict */
misra-c2012-8.14.pitfalls: Removing restrict may reduce compiler optimization opportunities.
misra-c2012-8.14.context_notes: MISRA forbids restrict; if performance is critical, document the deviation.

misra-c2012-9.1.fix: Initialize the variable at declaration or on all paths before first use.
misra-c2012-9.1.example: int result = 0; /* fix: misra-c2012-9.1 — initialized at declaration */
misra-c2012-9.1.caution: Choose an appropriate initial value; zero may mask logic errors.
misra-c2012-9.1.pitfalls: If the variable is set in multiple branches, ensure every branch assigns before use.
misra-c2012-9.1.context_notes: In safety-critical code, uninitialized reads are undefined behavior and may cause unpredictable results.

misra-c2012-9.2.fix: Use fully brace-enclosed initializer lists for arrays and structs.
misra-c2012-9.2.example: int arr[3] = {1, 2, 3}; /* fix: misra-c2012-9.2 — brace-enclosed init */
misra-c2012-9.2.caution: Ensure the number of initializer elements matches the array/struct size.

misra-c2012-9.3.fix: Either initialize all array elements explicitly or use {0} for zero-initialization.
misra-c2012-9.3.example: int arr[4] = {0}; /* fix: misra-c2012-9.3 — zero-initialized all elements */
misra-c2012-9.3.caution: Partial initialization may silently zero-fill remaining elements; verify intent.

misra-c2012-9.4.fix: Remove duplicate initializer for the same element.
misra-c2012-9.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-9.4 — removed duplicate initializer for element [2] */
misra-c2012-9.4.caution: In C99 designated initializers, later values override earlier ones; verify intent.

misra-c2012-9.5.fix: Use an explicit array size instead of relying on initializer count.
misra-c2012-9.5.example: int arr[3] = {1, 2, 3}; /* fix: misra-c2012-9.5 — explicit size */
misra-c2012-9.5.caution: The explicit size must match the actual number of initializer elements.

misra-c2012-10.1.fix: Add an explicit cast or use an operand of the correct essential type.
misra-c2012-10.1.example: uint32_t r = (uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)b; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.1 — explicit cast */
misra-c2012-10.1.caution: Ensure the cast does not cause data truncation or unexpected sign extension.

misra-c2012-10.2.fix: Do not use char type in arithmetic; cast to an appropriate integer type.
misra-c2012-10.2.example: int offset = (int)ch - (int)'A'; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.2 — explicit int cast */
misra-c2012-10.2.pitfalls: The sign of plain char is implementation-defined; casting to int may produce negative values.
misra-c2012-10.2.context_notes: Use unsigned char for byte arithmetic to avoid sign issues.

misra-c2012-10.3.fix: Add an explicit cast when assigning to a narrower or different essential type.
misra-c2012-10.3.example: uint8_t val = (uint8_t)wide_val; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.3 — explicit narrowing cast */
misra-c2012-10.3.caution: Verify the value fits in the target type; narrowing may lose data.

misra-c2012-10.4.fix: Ensure both operands of arithmetic/comparison have the same essential type.
misra-c2012-10.4.example: if ((uint32_t)a == (uint32_t)b) /* fix: misra-c2012-10.4 — same essential type */
misra-c2012-10.4.caution: Casting to a wider type may hide logic errors if the original types differ intentionally.

misra-c2012-10.5.fix: Replace the inappropriate cast with one between compatible essential types.
misra-c2012-10.5.example: uint8_t flags = (uint8_t)(reg & 0xFFU); /* fix: misra-c2012-10.5 — appropriate cast */
misra-c2012-10.5.caution: Do not cast between boolean, enum, and integer types without review.

misra-c2012-10.6.fix: Assign the composite expression result to the correct width type directly.
misra-c2012-10.6.example: uint32_t r = (uint32_t)a * (uint32_t)b; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.6 — widen before op */
misra-c2012-10.6.caution: Widening after the operation does not prevent intermediate overflow.

misra-c2012-10.7.fix: Cast an operand to the wider type before the arithmetic operation.
misra-c2012-10.7.example: uint32_t r = (uint32_t)u16a + (uint32_t)u16b; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.7 — widen before op */
misra-c2012-10.7.caution: The wider type must be chosen to avoid both overflow and sign issues.

misra-c2012-10.8.fix: Avoid casting a composite expression to a different essential type category; restructure.
misra-c2012-10.8.example: uint32_t tmp = a + b; int32_t r = (int32_t)tmp; /* fix: misra-c2012-10.8 — separate cast */
misra-c2012-10.8.pitfalls: Complex type conversions can mask overflow or sign-change bugs.
misra-c2012-10.8.context_notes: Prefer step-by-step casts through intermediate variables for clarity.

misra-c2012-11.1.fix: Do not convert between function pointer and other pointer/integer types.
misra-c2012-11.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-11.1 — removed function pointer to void* cast */
misra-c2012-11.1.pitfalls: Function pointer casts can cause undefined behavior if the signature does not match.
misra-c2012-11.1.context_notes: If a callback registry requires void*, use a wrapper struct instead of casting.

misra-c2012-11.2.fix: Do not convert between pointer to incomplete type and other pointer types.
misra-c2012-11.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-11.2 — used complete type definition before cast */
misra-c2012-11.2.pitfalls: Incomplete type casts can cause alignment and size assumptions to be wrong.
misra-c2012-11.2.context_notes: Provide the full struct definition in a shared header before casting.

misra-c2012-11.3.fix: Add explicit cast between object pointer types with a justifying comment.
misra-c2012-11.3.caution: Verify target type alignment requirements are satisfied.

misra-c2012-11.4.fix: Use uintptr_t as an intermediate for integer-to-pointer conversions.

misra-c2012-11.4.context_notes: In embedded code, document the hardware register address and access width.

misra-c2012-11.5.fix: Add explicit cast from void* to the target object pointer type.
misra-c2012-11.5.example: uint8_t *buf = (uint8_t *)malloc(n); /* fix: misra-c2012-11.5 — explicit void* cast */
misra-c2012-11.5.caution: Verify alignment requirements of the target type.

misra-c2012-11.6.fix: Do not cast between void* and an arithmetic type; use uintptr_t if needed.
misra-c2012-11.6.example: uintptr_t val = (uintptr_t)ptr; /* fix: misra-c2012-11.6 — via uintptr_t */
misra-c2012-11.6.pitfalls: Pointer-to-integer and integer-to-pointer casts are implementation-defined.
misra-c2012-11.6.context_notes: Only use this pattern for hardware register addresses or debug output.

misra-c2012-11.7.fix: Do not cast between object pointer and non-integer arithmetic type.

misra-c2012-11.7.pitfalls: This type of cast produces undefined behavior in all cases.
misra-c2012-11.7.context_notes: Use memcpy for type-punning between pointer and non-integer types.

misra-c2012-11.8.fix: Do not cast away const or volatile qualifiers.
misra-c2012-11.8.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-11.8 — preserved const qualifier in cast */
misra-c2012-11.8.caution: If removing const is required for legacy APIs, isolate and document the deviation.

misra-c2012-11.9.fix: Use the NULL macro (not integer 0) as the null pointer constant.
misra-c2012-11.9.example: ptr = NULL; /* fix: misra-c2012-11.9 — use NULL macro */

misra-c2012-12.1.fix: Add explicit parentheses to clarify operator precedence.
misra-c2012-12.1.example: result = (a + b) * c; /* fix: misra-c2012-12.1 — added clarifying parentheses */
misra-c2012-12.1.caution: Verify the parenthesization matches the intended evaluation order.

misra-c2012-12.2.fix: Ensure the shift amount is non-negative and less than the bit width of the type.
misra-c2012-12.2.example: uint32_t r = val << 4U; /* fix: misra-c2012-12.2 — shift within bit width */
misra-c2012-12.2.pitfalls: Shifting by a negative amount or beyond the type width is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-12.2.context_notes: Add a compile-time or runtime check for the shift amount if it comes from a variable.

misra-c2012-12.3.fix: Replace the comma operator with separate statements.
misra-c2012-12.3.example: a = 1; b = 2; /* fix: misra-c2012-12.3 — separated comma expression into statements */
misra-c2012-12.3.caution: In for-loop headers, the comma operator is common; restructure the loop if needed.

misra-c2012-12.4.fix: Ensure constant expressions used in preprocessor or array sizes have no side effects.
misra-c2012-12.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-12.4 — replaced runtime expression with compile-time constant */
misra-c2012-12.4.pitfalls: Expressions that appear constant may depend on volatile or function calls.
misra-c2012-12.4.context_notes: Use enum or #define for compile-time constants instead of const variables.

misra-c2012-12.5.fix: Do not apply sizeof to an array-typed function parameter (it gives pointer size).
misra-c2012-12.5.example: #define ARRAY_LEN(a) (sizeof(a)/sizeof((a)[0])) /* fix: misra-c2012-12.5 — use macro at caller */
misra-c2012-12.5.caution: Pass the array size as a separate parameter to the function.

misra-c2012-13.1.fix: Move expressions with side effects out of the initializer list.
misra-c2012-13.1.example: int v = get_val(); int arr[] = {v, 0}; /* fix: misra-c2012-13.1 — side effect before init */
misra-c2012-13.1.pitfalls: Evaluation order of initializer list elements is not fully specified in C.
misra-c2012-13.1.context_notes: In safety-critical code, initializer lists should only contain constants or simple variables.

misra-c2012-13.2.fix: Split the expression so each statement has at most one side effect.
misra-c2012-13.2.example: tmp = f(); result = tmp + g(); /* fix: misra-c2012-13.2 — one side effect per statement */
misra-c2012-13.2.pitfalls: Unsequenced side effects cause undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-13.2.context_notes: Compilers may reorder sub-expressions; splitting ensures deterministic evaluation.

misra-c2012-13.3.fix: Separate increment/decrement operations from other expressions.
misra-c2012-13.3.example: i++; arr[i] = val; /* fix: misra-c2012-13.3 — separated increment from use */
misra-c2012-13.3.caution: Verify the intended evaluation order after separation.

misra-c2012-13.4.fix: Move the assignment out of the controlling expression (if/while/for condition).
misra-c2012-13.4.example: val = get(); if (val != 0) { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-13.4 — assignment before condition */
misra-c2012-13.4.caution: For while-loop patterns, use an explicit assignment inside the loop body.

misra-c2012-13.5.fix: Move expressions with persistent side effects out of the right-hand side of && or ||.
misra-c2012-13.5.example: flag = has_data(); if (ready && flag) { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-13.5 — pre-evaluated RHS */
misra-c2012-13.5.caution: Short-circuit evaluation means the RHS may not execute; pre-evaluation changes this.

misra-c2012-13.6.fix: Remove expressions with side effects from the sizeof operand.
misra-c2012-13.6.example: size_t s = sizeof(int); /* fix: misra-c2012-13.6 — removed side effect from sizeof */

misra-c2012-14.1.fix: Replace the floating-point loop counter with an integer counter.
misra-c2012-14.1.example: for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) /* fix: misra-c2012-14.1 — integer loop counter */
misra-c2012-14.1.pitfalls: Floating-point comparison in loop conditions can cause infinite loops due to precision.
misra-c2012-14.1.context_notes: In timing-critical loops, integer counters are both safer and faster.

misra-c2012-14.2.fix: Ensure the for-loop has a single counter, a proper bound test, and a simple increment.
misra-c2012-14.2.example: for (uint8_t i = 0U; i < n; i++) /* fix: misra-c2012-14.2 — well-formed for loop */
misra-c2012-14.2.caution: Do not modify the loop counter inside the loop body.

misra-c2012-14.3.fix: Review and fix the controlling expression that is always true or always false.
misra-c2012-14.3.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-14.3 — replaced invariant condition with runtime check */
misra-c2012-14.3.pitfalls: An always-true condition may indicate a logic error or missing variable update.
misra-c2012-14.3.context_notes: In defensive code, intentional infinite loops (while(1)) should use a documented deviation.

misra-c2012-14.4.fix: Use an explicit boolean comparison instead of implicit truthiness.
misra-c2012-14.4.example: if (flag != 0U) /* fix: misra-c2012-14.4 — explicit boolean test */
misra-c2012-14.4.caution: For pointer checks, use (ptr != NULL) instead of (ptr).

misra-c2012-15.1.fix: Replace goto with structured control flow (if/else, break, return, flag variable).

misra-c2012-15.1.context_notes: In error-cleanup idioms, a single goto-cleanup may be acceptable with a documented deviation.

misra-c2012-15.2.fix: Ensure goto jumps to a label later in the same or an enclosing block.

misra-c2012-15.2.pitfalls: Backward jumps can create implicit loops that bypass initialization.
misra-c2012-15.2.context_notes: Consider replacing with a do-while or state machine pattern.

misra-c2012-15.3.fix: Ensure the goto label is in the same block or an enclosing block as the goto statement.

misra-c2012-15.3.pitfalls: Cross-block jumps can skip variable initialization and resource acquisition.
misra-c2012-15.3.context_notes: Restructure using a flag variable or separate function to avoid cross-block goto.

misra-c2012-15.4.fix: Ensure at most one break or goto statement per loop.
misra-c2012-15.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-15.4 — consolidated multiple breaks into single exit condition */
misra-c2012-15.4.pitfalls: Merging break conditions may change the loop's iteration behavior.
misra-c2012-15.4.context_notes: Use a found/done flag to combine multiple exit conditions into one break.

misra-c2012-15.5.fix: Restructure the function to have a single point of return.
misra-c2012-15.5.example: int result = ERR; /* ... */ return result; /* fix: misra-c2012-15.5 — single return */
misra-c2012-15.5.caution: Single-return may require deeper nesting; balance readability with compliance.

misra-c2012-15.6.fix: Add braces around the body of if, else, while, for, do, and switch statements.
misra-c2012-15.6.example: if (x > 0) { y = x; } /* fix: misra-c2012-15.6 — added compound statement */

misra-c2012-15.7.fix: Add a final else clause to an if-else-if chain.
misra-c2012-15.7.example: if (a) { ... } else if (b) { ... } else { /* default */ } /* fix: misra-c2012-15.7 — added else */

misra-c2012-16.1.fix: Ensure the switch body is a well-formed compound statement with only case/default labels.
misra-c2012-16.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-16.1 — restructured switch to well-formed block */
misra-c2012-16.1.caution: Do not place declarations or executable code before the first case label.

misra-c2012-16.2.fix: Move case and default labels to the top level of the switch statement (no nested cases).
misra-c2012-16.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-16.2 — moved case label to switch top level */
misra-c2012-16.2.pitfalls: Duff's device and similar patterns violate this rule and must be refactored.
misra-c2012-16.2.context_notes: Use separate functions for complex cases to keep the switch structure flat.

misra-c2012-16.3.fix: Add break (or return) at the end of every switch case clause.
misra-c2012-16.3.example: case 1: handle_one(); break; /* fix: misra-c2012-16.3 — added break */
misra-c2012-16.3.caution: If fallthrough is intentional, restructure to avoid it or document a deviation.

misra-c2012-16.4.fix: Add a default case to the switch statement.
misra-c2012-16.4.example: default: break; /* fix: misra-c2012-16.4 — added default case */

misra-c2012-16.5.fix: Move the default case to the last position in the switch statement.
misra-c2012-16.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-16.5 — moved default to last position */

misra-c2012-16.6.fix: Ensure the switch statement has at least two case clauses (otherwise use if).
misra-c2012-16.6.example: if (val == 1) { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-16.6 — replaced trivial switch with if */
misra-c2012-16.6.caution: If more cases are expected in the future, document why the switch is kept.

misra-c2012-16.7.fix: Replace a switch on a boolean expression with an if-else.
misra-c2012-16.7.example: if (flag) { ... } else { ... } /* fix: misra-c2012-16.7 — replaced boolean switch with if */
misra-c2012-16.7.caution: Verify the switch expression is truly boolean and not an enum with two values.

misra-c2012-17.1.fix: Do not use <stdarg.h> or variadic functions (va_list, va_start, va_arg, va_end).
misra-c2012-17.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-17.1 — replaced variadic function with fixed-parameter version */
misra-c2012-17.1.pitfalls: Variadic functions bypass type checking and can cause stack corruption.
misra-c2012-17.1.context_notes: Use arrays or structs to pass variable numbers of arguments safely.

misra-c2012-17.2.fix: Remove direct or indirect recursion; use iteration or an explicit stack.
misra-c2012-17.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-17.2 — replaced recursion with iterative loop */
misra-c2012-17.2.pitfalls: Recursion removal may require an explicit stack data structure.
misra-c2012-17.2.context_notes: In embedded systems, recursion risks stack overflow with limited stack space.

misra-c2012-17.3.fix: Add a proper declaration or #include for the function before the call.
misra-c2012-17.3.example: #include "module.h" /* fix: misra-c2012-17.3 — added declaration via include */
misra-c2012-17.3.caution: Implicit function declarations assume int return type, which may be wrong.

misra-c2012-17.4.fix: Add a NULL check for the pointer parameter before dereferencing.
misra-c2012-17.4.example: if (p == NULL) { return ERR; } /* fix: misra-c2012-17.4 — NULL check for parameter */
misra-c2012-17.4.caution: Determine whether returning an error or asserting is more appropriate.

misra-c2012-17.5.fix: Specify the array dimension in the function parameter declaration.
misra-c2012-17.5.example: void process(uint8_t data[DATA_SIZE]); /* fix: misra-c2012-17.5 — added dimension */
misra-c2012-17.5.caution: The dimension is for documentation only; it does not prevent out-of-bounds access.

misra-c2012-17.6.fix: Do not modify the address stored in an array parameter.
misra-c2012-17.6.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-17.6 — used index instead of modifying array parameter pointer */
misra-c2012-17.6.pitfalls: Pointer arithmetic on array parameters obscures the original array base address.

misra-c2012-17.7.fix: Use the return value, or explicitly cast to (void) if intentionally discarding.
misra-c2012-17.7.example: (void)memset(buf, 0, sz); /* fix: misra-c2012-17.7 — cast unused return to void */
misra-c2012-17.7.caution: Silently discarding return values may hide errors.
misra-c2012-17.7.pitfalls: If the function can fail, prefer capturing and checking the return value rather than (void) cast.
misra-c2012-17.7.context_notes: In safety-critical code, capture the return value and handle errors explicitly.

misra-c2012-17.8.fix: Do not modify a function parameter; copy it to a local variable first.
misra-c2012-17.8.example: int local = param; local++; /* fix: misra-c2012-17.8 — local copy, not modify param */
misra-c2012-17.8.caution: Ensure the local copy is used consistently throughout the function.

misra-c2012-18.1.fix: Add a bounds check before pointer arithmetic to ensure it stays within the array.
misra-c2012-18.1.example: if (idx < arr_size) { val = arr[idx]; } /* fix: misra-c2012-18.1 — bounds check */
misra-c2012-18.1.pitfalls: Pointer arithmetic beyond the array bounds (even without dereference) is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-18.1.context_notes: Prefer array indexing over pointer arithmetic for clarity.

misra-c2012-18.2.fix: Ensure pointer subtraction is only performed on pointers to the same array.
misra-c2012-18.2.example: ptrdiff_t d = &arr[i] - &arr[0]; /* fix: misra-c2012-18.2 — same array origin */
misra-c2012-18.2.pitfalls: Subtracting pointers to different objects is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-18.2.context_notes: Use index arithmetic instead of pointer subtraction when possible.

misra-c2012-18.3.fix: Ensure pointer comparison (< > <= >=) is only between pointers to the same array.
misra-c2012-18.3.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-18.3 — restructured to compare indices instead of pointers */
misra-c2012-18.3.pitfalls: Comparing pointers to different objects is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-18.3.context_notes: Use index comparison instead of pointer comparison.

misra-c2012-18.4.fix: Replace pointer arithmetic (+, -, +=, -=) with array indexing.
misra-c2012-18.4.example: val = arr[offset]; /* fix: misra-c2012-18.4 — array index instead of *(arr + offset) */
misra-c2012-18.4.caution: Verify the index calculation is equivalent to the original pointer arithmetic.

misra-c2012-18.5.fix: Limit pointer indirection to at most two levels.
misra-c2012-18.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-18.5 — refactored to reduce pointer indirection depth */
misra-c2012-18.5.caution: Reducing indirection may require structural changes to data types.

misra-c2012-18.6.fix: Do not use the address of an automatic variable after its scope ends; copy the data.
misra-c2012-18.6.example: memcpy(out, &local, sizeof(local)); /* fix: misra-c2012-18.6 — copied data before scope exit */
misra-c2012-18.6.caution: Ensure the destination buffer is large enough for the copied data.

misra-c2012-18.7.fix: Replace flexible array member with a fixed-size array.
misra-c2012-18.7.example: uint8_t data[MAX_DATA_SIZE]; /* fix: misra-c2012-18.7 — fixed-size array */

misra-c2012-18.8.fix: Replace variable-length array (VLA) with a fixed-size array or dynamic allocation.
misra-c2012-18.8.example: uint8_t buf[MAX_BUF]; /* fix: misra-c2012-18.8 — fixed-size array instead of VLA */

misra-c2012-19.1.fix: Avoid assigning between overlapping objects; use a temporary or memcpy.
misra-c2012-19.1.example: memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(dst)); /* fix: misra-c2012-19.1 — safe copy via memcpy */
misra-c2012-19.1.pitfalls: Direct assignment of overlapping objects (e.g., union members) is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-19.1.context_notes: Use memmove instead of memcpy if the memory regions may overlap.

misra-c2012-19.2.fix: Replace union with a struct containing a type tag and separate members.
misra-c2012-19.2.example: struct Tagged { int type; uint8_t byte_val; uint32_t word_val; }; /* fix: misra-c2012-19.2 — tagged struct */
misra-c2012-19.2.pitfalls: Unions allow type punning, which is undefined behavior except for specific cases.
misra-c2012-19.2.context_notes: If union is required for hardware register mapping, document a deviation.

misra-c2012-20.1.fix: Ensure only preprocessor directives and comments precede #include directives.
misra-c2012-20.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.1 — moved code after #include block */
misra-c2012-20.1.caution: Some code generators place declarations before includes; restructure if possible.

misra-c2012-20.2.fix: Remove ', ", \, /*, or // characters from #include header names.

misra-c2012-20.3.fix: Ensure #include resolves to an actual source file in the include path.
misra-c2012-20.3.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.3 — verified include path resolves correctly */
misra-c2012-20.3.caution: Check that the include search path is correctly configured in the build system.

misra-c2012-20.4.fix: Do not define a macro with the same name as a C keyword or standard library identifier.
misra-c2012-20.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.4 — renamed macro to avoid keyword collision */
misra-c2012-20.4.pitfalls: Redefining keywords can cause subtle compilation or behavior differences across compilers.
misra-c2012-20.4.context_notes: Use a project-specific prefix for all macros to avoid collisions.

misra-c2012-20.5.fix: Do not use #undef; use conditional compilation or separate macro names instead.
misra-c2012-20.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.5 — removed #undef, used MODULE_FEATURE_V2 instead */
misra-c2012-20.5.caution: Removing #undef may expose the original macro in unexpected scopes.

misra-c2012-20.6.fix: Ensure token pasting (##) and stringification (#) produce valid tokens.
misra-c2012-20.6.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.6 — restructured macro for well-formed token pasting */
misra-c2012-20.6.caution: Token pasting that produces an invalid token is undefined behavior.

misra-c2012-20.7.fix: Parenthesize all macro parameters used in the expansion.

misra-c2012-20.8.fix: Ensure #if/#elif controlling expression is well-formed and evaluates correctly.
misra-c2012-20.8.caution: Undefined macros in #if evaluate to 0, which may be unintentional.

misra-c2012-20.9.fix: Define the macro before using it in #if; do not rely on undefined-macro-is-0 behavior.
misra-c2012-20.9.example: #if defined(CFG_FLAG) && (CFG_FLAG == 1) /* fix: misra-c2012-20.9 — guarded with defined() */

misra-c2012-20.10.fix: Avoid # (stringification) and ## (token pasting); prefer inline functions or enums.
misra-c2012-20.10.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.10 — replaced macro with inline function */
misra-c2012-20.10.caution: Some debug/logging macros legitimately need # for stringification; document deviation.

misra-c2012-20.11.fix: Do not use more than one # or ## operator in a single macro definition.
misra-c2012-20.11.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.11 — split macro into two simpler macros */
misra-c2012-20.11.caution: Splitting macros may affect the expansion behavior; verify in all use sites.

misra-c2012-20.12.fix: Ensure each macro parameter is used at most once per expansion (avoid side-effect duplication).
misra-c2012-20.12.example: #define MAX(a, b) _max_impl((a), (b)) /* fix: misra-c2012-20.12 — delegate to inline function */
misra-c2012-20.12.caution: Macro parameters expanded multiple times will evaluate side effects multiple times.

misra-c2012-20.13.fix: Ensure preprocessor directives do not end with a backslash continuation.
misra-c2012-20.13.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-20.13 — removed trailing backslash from directive */

misra-c2012-20.14.fix: Use #if defined(X) syntax with parentheses instead of #ifdef or bare #if defined X.
misra-c2012-20.14.example: #if defined(FEATURE) /* fix: misra-c2012-20.14 — used defined() with parentheses */

misra-c2012-21.1.fix: Do not #define or #undef identifiers that start with underscore or match reserved names.
misra-c2012-21.1.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.1 — renamed macro to avoid reserved namespace */
misra-c2012-21.1.pitfalls: Redefining reserved identifiers causes undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-21.1.context_notes: Use a project-specific prefix (e.g., APP_ or MOD_) for all macros.

misra-c2012-21.2.fix: Do not declare identifiers with names reserved by the standard library.
misra-c2012-21.2.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.2 — renamed to avoid reserved identifier conflict */
misra-c2012-21.2.pitfalls: Colliding with standard library names can silently change program behavior.
misra-c2012-21.2.context_notes: Check both C standard reserved names and POSIX reserved patterns.

misra-c2012-21.3.fix: Replace malloc/calloc/realloc/free with static allocation or pre-allocated pools.
misra-c2012-21.3.example: static uint8_t pool[POOL_SIZE]; /* fix: misra-c2012-21.3 — static allocation */
misra-c2012-21.3.pitfalls: Static allocation requires knowing the maximum size at compile time.
misra-c2012-21.3.context_notes: In AUTOSAR/safety-critical systems, dynamic allocation is forbidden by standard.

misra-c2012-21.4.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.4 — replaced setjmp/longjmp with structured error handling */
misra-c2012-21.4.pitfalls: setjmp/longjmp bypass destructors and cleanup code.
misra-c2012-21.4.context_notes: Use error codes and return-value propagation for non-local error handling.

misra-c2012-21.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.5 — replaced signal handling with polling or event flag */
misra-c2012-21.5.pitfalls: Signal handlers have severe restrictions on what operations are safe.
misra-c2012-21.5.context_notes: In embedded systems, use hardware interrupt handlers instead of POSIX signals.

misra-c2012-21.6.fix: Do not use <stdio.h> for I/O in production code; use platform-specific alternatives.
misra-c2012-21.6.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.6 — replaced printf with platform-specific debug output */
misra-c2012-21.6.pitfalls: stdio functions may use dynamic allocation and are not reentrant.
misra-c2012-21.6.context_notes: For debug builds, wrap stdio usage in #ifdef DEBUG guards.

misra-c2012-21.7.fix: Replace atof/atoi/atol with strtol/strtod and check for conversion errors.
misra-c2012-21.7.example: long val = strtol(str, &end, 10); /* fix: misra-c2012-21.7 — strtol with error check */
misra-c2012-21.7.pitfalls: ato* functions have undefined behavior on out-of-range input.
misra-c2012-21.7.context_notes: Always check the end pointer and errno after strto* calls.

misra-c2012-21.8.fix: Do not use abort/exit/getenv/system; use platform-specific alternatives.
misra-c2012-21.8.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.8 — replaced exit() with controlled shutdown sequence */
misra-c2012-21.8.pitfalls: abort() and exit() bypass normal cleanup; getenv() is not thread-safe.
misra-c2012-21.8.context_notes: In embedded systems, implement a controlled shutdown or reset procedure.

misra-c2012-21.9.fix: Do not use bsearch/qsort from <stdlib.h>; use custom implementations.
misra-c2012-21.9.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.9 — replaced qsort with custom insertion sort */
misra-c2012-21.9.pitfalls: Standard library sort/search may use recursion or dynamic allocation internally.
misra-c2012-21.9.context_notes: Custom implementations allow control over stack usage and comparison behavior.

misra-c2012-21.10.fix: Do not use <time.h> date/time functions; use platform-specific time API.
misra-c2012-21.10.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.10 — replaced time() with platform-specific RTC read */
misra-c2012-21.10.pitfalls: Standard time functions may not be available or accurate on embedded targets.
misra-c2012-21.10.context_notes: Use hardware timer or RTC peripherals for timing in embedded systems.

misra-c2012-21.11.fix: Do not use <tgmath.h>; use explicit math function variants (sinf, sin, sinl).
misra-c2012-21.11.example: float r = sinf(x); /* fix: misra-c2012-21.11 — explicit single-precision sinf */
misra-c2012-21.11.pitfalls: Type-generic macros may select unexpected precision at compile time.
misra-c2012-21.11.context_notes: Always use the explicitly-typed math function matching your variable type.

misra-c2012-21.12.fix: Do not use <fenv.h> floating-point environment functions except feclearexcept/fetestexcept.
misra-c2012-21.12.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.12 — removed fesetround, using compile-time rounding mode */
misra-c2012-21.12.pitfalls: Floating-point environment changes are global state and affect all FP operations.
misra-c2012-21.12.context_notes: Use compiler pragmas or attributes for rounding mode control if needed.

misra-c2012-21.13.fix: Cast the argument to (unsigned char) before passing to ctype.h functions.
misra-c2012-21.13.example: if (isalpha((unsigned char)c)) /* fix: misra-c2012-21.13 — unsigned char cast */
misra-c2012-21.13.caution: Plain char may be signed; passing negative values to ctype functions is undefined.

misra-c2012-21.14.fix: Do not use memcmp to compare strings; use strcmp or strncmp.
misra-c2012-21.14.example: if (strcmp(a, b) == 0) /* fix: misra-c2012-21.14 — strcmp instead of memcmp for strings */
misra-c2012-21.14.pitfalls: memcmp compares bytes beyond the null terminator, which may give wrong results.
misra-c2012-21.14.context_notes: Use strncmp with a length limit for bounded string comparison.

misra-c2012-21.15.fix: Ensure both pointer arguments to memcpy/memmove/memcmp point to compatible types.
misra-c2012-21.15.example: memcpy(dst_arr, src_arr, sizeof(dst_arr)); /* fix: misra-c2012-21.15 — compatible types */
misra-c2012-21.15.caution: If types differ, use an explicit intermediate cast with a comment explaining why.

misra-c2012-21.16.fix: Ensure both pointer arguments to memcmp point to objects of the same type.
misra-c2012-21.16.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.16 — ensured both memcmp arguments are same type */
misra-c2012-21.16.pitfalls: Comparing different types via memcmp may give platform-dependent results due to padding.
misra-c2012-21.16.context_notes: For struct comparison, compare member by member instead of using memcmp.

misra-c2012-21.17.fix: Ensure the destination buffer is large enough for the string operation (including null terminator).
misra-c2012-21.17.example: strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst) - 1U); dst[sizeof(dst) - 1U] = '\0'; /* fix: misra-c2012-21.17 — bounded copy */
misra-c2012-21.17.pitfalls: strcpy and strcat do not check bounds; always use bounded variants.
misra-c2012-21.17.context_notes: Prefer snprintf for formatted string operations with automatic bounds checking.

misra-c2012-21.18.fix: Ensure the size_t argument to string functions does not exceed the buffer size.
misra-c2012-21.18.example: memset(buf, 0, sizeof(buf)); /* fix: misra-c2012-21.18 — size matches buffer */
misra-c2012-21.18.pitfalls: Passing a size larger than the buffer causes buffer overflow.
misra-c2012-21.18.context_notes: Use sizeof(buf) instead of hardcoded constants for buffer sizes.

misra-c2012-21.19.fix: Do not store a pointer to a string literal in a non-const-qualified pointer.
misra-c2012-21.19.example: const char *msg = "hello"; /* fix: misra-c2012-21.19 — const pointer for literal */

misra-c2012-21.20.fix: Store the return value of string functions before the next call that may invalidate it.
misra-c2012-21.20.example: char *s1 = strdup(strtok(NULL, ",")); /* fix: misra-c2012-21.20 — saved before next call */
misra-c2012-21.20.caution: Functions like strtok, asctime, and strerror return pointers to static buffers.

misra-c2012-21.21.fix: Do not use system(); use platform-specific process or command API.
misra-c2012-21.21.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-21.21 — replaced system() with platform-specific API */
misra-c2012-21.21.pitfalls: system() is a security risk (command injection) and is not available on all targets.
misra-c2012-21.21.context_notes: In embedded systems, there is typically no shell to execute commands.

misra-c2012-22.1.fix: Ensure every opened file is closed on all code paths, including error paths.
misra-c2012-22.1.example: fclose(fp); /* fix: misra-c2012-22.1 — added fclose on error path */
misra-c2012-22.1.pitfalls: Missing fclose on error paths causes resource leaks that may exhaust file descriptors.
misra-c2012-22.1.context_notes: Use a goto-cleanup pattern to centralize resource release.

misra-c2012-22.2.fix: Only close a file that was successfully opened; check the file pointer first.
misra-c2012-22.2.example: if (fp != NULL) { fclose(fp); } /* fix: misra-c2012-22.2 — guarded fclose */
misra-c2012-22.2.pitfalls: Closing a NULL or invalid file pointer is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-22.2.context_notes: Set file pointer to NULL after close to prevent double-close.

misra-c2012-22.3.fix: Do not open the same file for both read and write simultaneously from different streams.
misra-c2012-22.3.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.3 — serialized file access: read then write */
misra-c2012-22.3.pitfalls: Concurrent read/write to the same file can produce inconsistent data.
misra-c2012-22.3.context_notes: Use file locking or serialize access if concurrent access is unavoidable.

misra-c2012-22.4.fix: Do not write to a file opened in read-only mode; open with appropriate mode.
misra-c2012-22.4.example: fp = fopen(path, "r+"); /* fix: misra-c2012-22.4 — opened with read-write mode */
misra-c2012-22.4.pitfalls: Writing to a read-only file is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-22.4.context_notes: Use the minimum required access mode to reduce risk.

misra-c2012-22.5.fix: Do not dereference a FILE* pointer directly; use only standard I/O functions.
misra-c2012-22.5.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.5 — used fread instead of direct FILE struct access */
misra-c2012-22.5.pitfalls: FILE struct layout is implementation-defined; direct access is non-portable.

misra-c2012-22.6.fix: Do not use a FILE* after it has been closed; set to NULL after fclose.
misra-c2012-22.6.example: fclose(fp); fp = NULL; /* fix: misra-c2012-22.6 — set NULL after close */
misra-c2012-22.6.pitfalls: Using a closed file pointer is undefined behavior.
misra-c2012-22.6.context_notes: Setting to NULL enables runtime detection of use-after-close bugs.

misra-c2012-22.7.fix: Do not compare EOF with a char variable; use int type for the result of getc/fgetc.
misra-c2012-22.7.example: int c = fgetc(fp); if (c == EOF) /* fix: misra-c2012-22.7 — int type for EOF check */
misra-c2012-22.7.pitfalls: EOF is negative; storing in unsigned char loses the EOF signal.

misra-c2012-22.8.fix: Set errno to zero immediately before calling a function that sets errno.
misra-c2012-22.8.example: errno = 0; val = strtol(str, &end, 10); /* fix: misra-c2012-22.8 — cleared errno */
misra-c2012-22.8.pitfalls: Stale errno values from previous calls can cause false error detection.
misra-c2012-22.8.context_notes: Always pair errno = 0 with the subsequent function call in a single code block.

misra-c2012-22.9.fix: Check errno after calling a function that may set it on error.
misra-c2012-22.9.example: if (errno != 0) { handle_error(); } /* fix: misra-c2012-22.9 — checked errno after call */
misra-c2012-22.9.pitfalls: Some functions set errno even on success; check both return value and errno.
misra-c2012-22.9.context_notes: Consult the function documentation for which errno values indicate true errors.

misra-c2012-22.10.fix: Only check errno after functions that are documented to set it.
misra-c2012-22.10.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.10 — removed errno check after function that does not set it */
misra-c2012-22.10.pitfalls: Checking errno after a non-errno-setting function reads a stale value.
misra-c2012-22.10.context_notes: Refer to the C standard or POSIX specification for which functions set errno.

misra-c2012-22.11.fix: Do not use tss_get; use platform-specific thread-local storage API.
misra-c2012-22.11.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.11 — replaced tss_get with platform TLS API */
misra-c2012-22.11.pitfalls: C11 thread support is optional and may not be available on all platforms.

misra-c2012-22.12.fix: Do not use mtx_timedlock; use platform-specific timed mutex API.
misra-c2012-22.12.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.12 — replaced mtx_timedlock with platform mutex API */
misra-c2012-22.12.pitfalls: C11 thread support is optional and may not be available on all platforms.

misra-c2012-22.13.fix: Ensure file resources are closed on error paths, not just the success path.
misra-c2012-22.13.example: if (err) { fclose(fp); return ERR; } /* fix: misra-c2012-22.13 — close on error path */
misra-c2012-22.13.pitfalls: Early returns may skip cleanup code; use goto-cleanup pattern for multiple resources.
misra-c2012-22.13.context_notes: Review all error paths to ensure no resource leak.

misra-c2012-22.14.fix: Do not share a FILE* across threads; use thread-local file handles.
misra-c2012-22.14.example: /* fix: misra-c2012-22.14 — moved FILE* to thread-local scope */
misra-c2012-22.14.pitfalls: Concurrent access to FILE* without synchronization causes data corruption.
misra-c2012-22.14.context_notes: If sharing is required, protect with a mutex and document the access pattern.

misra-c2012-22.15.fix: Verify the file mode string matches the intended operations (read, write, append).
misra-c2012-22.15.example: fp = fopen(path, "rb"); /* fix: misra-c2012-22.15 — correct binary read mode */
misra-c2012-22.15.pitfalls: Wrong file mode can cause silent data corruption or operation failure.

misra-c2012-22.16.fix: Do not use tmpfile() or tmpnam(); use mkstemp() or platform-specific secure temp file API.
misra-c2012-22.16.example: int fd = mkstemp(template); /* fix: misra-c2012-22.16 — secure temp file */
misra-c2012-22.16.pitfalls: tmpnam() has a TOCTOU race condition; tmpfile() may not be available on all platforms.

misra-c2012-22.17.fix: Do not pass the same pointer to realloc and assign back to it; use a separate variable.
misra-c2012-22.17.example: void *tmp = realloc(ptr, new_sz); if (tmp) { ptr = tmp; } /* fix: misra-c2012-22.17 — safe realloc */
misra-c2012-22.17.pitfalls: If realloc fails and you assigned to the same pointer, the original memory is leaked.
misra-c2012-22.17.context_notes: In safety-critical code, avoid realloc entirely; use static allocation.

misra-c2012-22.18.fix: Ensure dynamically allocated memory is freed on all code paths, including error paths.
misra-c2012-22.18.example: if (err) { free(buf); return ERR; } /* fix: misra-c2012-22.18 — free on error path */
misra-c2012-22.18.pitfalls: Missing free on error paths causes memory leaks that accumulate over time.
misra-c2012-22.18.context_notes: Use a goto-cleanup pattern to centralize memory release for multiple allocations.
